hypotheses.justification: hn is implied by hm except in one case, and in that case the conclusion holds trivially. (1) If m ≥ 1, then ‖1-n‖ = q^{-m} < 1 because q = absNorm v > 1. By the ultrametric inequality ‖n‖ = ‖1-(1-n)‖ = 1. (2) If m = 0, then ‖1-n‖ = 1. If ‖n‖ > 1, then ‖1-n‖ = ‖n‖ > 1, a contradiction, so ‖n‖ ≤ 1. If ‖n‖ = 1, the existing proof applies. If ‖n‖ < 1 (including n = 0), the conclusion is Ideal.absNorm v.asIdeal ^ min s 0 = 1, and it holds. By hc, v(c)^f = v(n) < 1, using that θ preserves the valuation, so ‖c‖ < 1. This follows from v_theta_eq_one for units, extended to all y by writing y as algebraMap(ϖ^k) times a unit, since θ fixes the base field. For ‖y‖ > 1 we get ‖θ y‖ = ‖y‖ > ‖c y‖, so ‖θ y - c y‖ = ‖y‖ > 1. Hence {y : (θ-c)y ∈ O} ∩ {y : π^s y ∈ O} = O, and the relative index of O in O is 1 = q^{min(s,0)}. The ‖n‖ < 1 case needs a separate short argument. So hn can be dropped, because m = 0 with n a non-unit gives index 1 anyway, and the proof would first derive hn1 by case analysis on m.
